test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 2 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A man has to cover a distance of 150 km in 12 hours. If he covers two-third of this distance in (5)/(8) of the time, then what should be his speed (in km/h, correct to one decimal place) to cover the remaining distance in the time left?
solution:
**Given:**

A man has to cover a distance of 150 km in 12 hours.

He covers two-third of this distance in (5)/(8) of the time.

**Concept used: **

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Two - third distance = dfrac{2}{3} x 150

⇒ 100 km

Time required to cover 100 km = dfrac{5}{8} x 12

⇒ 7.5 hours

Speed = dfrac{150 -100}{12 - 7.5} 

⇒ dfrac{50}{4.5} 

⇒ 11.1 km/h

**∴ His speed will be 11.1 km/h to cover the rest distance.**
